# Fix: handle \r\n line endings by replacing \r, and use correct column name "rep_name"
lines = real_content.replace('\r', '').strip().split('\n')
headers_list = [h.strip() for h in lines[0].split(',')]
print(f"Columns: {headers_list}")

target_reps = {"James Okafor", "Sofia Delgado"}
target_deals = {"D001", "D002", "D003", "D005", "D006", "D008"}

filtered_rows = []
for row_line in lines[1:]:
    cols = [c.strip() for c in row_line.split(',')]
    row = dict(zip(headers_list, cols))
    
    did = row.get("deal_id", "")
    rname = row.get("rep_name", "")
    st = row.get("status", "").lower()
    
    if did in target_deals and rname in target_reps and st == "won":
        filtered_rows.append(row)

print(f"\n{'='*95}")
print(f"Won Deals by James Okafor & Sofia Delgado — Deals D001, D002, D003, D005, D006, D008")

print(f"{'-'*95}")
for r in filtered_rows:
    print(f"{r['deal_id']:<10} {r['rep_name']:<20} {r['region']:<10} {r['product']:<25} {int(r['amount']):>10,} {r['close_date']:<12} {r['status']:<8}")

total_amount = sum(int(r['amount']) for r in filtered_rows)
print(f"{'-'*95}")
print(f"{'Total matching records:':<67} {len(filtered_rows)}")
